expectations.text: Signing the Best-tier commitments today on the strength of the waitlist and reactions is refused.
expectations.evidence: "❌ signing Best today".

expectations.text: An evidence ladder is applied, ranking opinion below stated interest below deposits or claimed tickets below actually showing up, with the waitlist signups and post reactions placed at stated interest.
expectations.evidence: Table: 3,000 reactions level 1 (opinion); 1,400 waitlist level 2 (stated interest); 60 tickets level 3.

expectations.text: Real claimed registrations are named as the required evidence before committing spend beyond the Good tier.
expectations.evidence: "Spend beyond the Good tier needs level 3, real registrations."

expectations.text: Committing Best-tier budget on stated-interest evidence is called out as premature scaling with a contract attached (or equivalent framing).
expectations.evidence: "premature scaling with a venue contract attached."

expectations.text: Budget-tier movement is keyed to written downgrade dates triggered by sponsorship revenue actually received by each date, not to waitlist size.
expectations.evidence: "driven by sponsorship revenue received by set dates, not by ticket pace."

expectations.text: Cancellation is rejected: a soft early-bird signal downgrades the tier (Best to Better to Good) instead of cancelling the event.
expectations.evidence: "A soft ticket signal downgrades the tier. It doesn't cancel the event."

expectations.text: The sponsorship-heavy funding model is used in the reasoning: with the bulk of budget targeted from sponsorship (around 80%+), viability is decoupled from ticket-sale velocity.
expectations.evidence: Cites the 80%+ sponsorship benchmark and that the ladder is driven by sponsor revenue, not ticket pace.

expectations.text: The 60 sold tickets are recognized as the strongest evidence class present - real claimed tickets - stronger than the 1,400-name waitlist.
expectations.evidence: Ladder places the 60 tickets at level 3, above the waitlist at level 2.

expectations.text: Ticket-sale pace checkpoints are treated as a trend to watch, not a go/no-go gate for the launch itself.
expectations.evidence: "The next move is a visibility push, not cancellation... a marketing gap, not a verdict on the market."

expectations.text: The premium catering and afterparty are identified as Best-tier headroom items - the first things a downgrade removes - rather than baseline commitments.
expectations.evidence: "Premium catering and a harbour-cruise afterparty are Best items."
